descriptionChirho: A military serviceman (στρατιώτης), a person serving in an army, used in both singular ('a soldier') and plural ('soldiers') forms throughout the NT narratives. Refers to Roman soldiers at the crucifixion, soldiers of Herod, soldiers guarding prisoners, and Paul's metaphorical 'fellow soldier.' Multilingual evidence is uniform across number: Arabic جُنْدِيّ (jundiyy, singular)/جُنُود (junūd, plural), Korean 군인/병사 (gunin/byeongsa, 'soldier'), Swahili askari ('soldier/guard'), Hindi सैनिक/सैनिकों (sainik/sainikoṃ), Spanish soldado/soldados. The singular and plural forms represent grammatical number inflection of one sense, not distinct lexicographic meanings.
